title: Consumer Response to Climate Change: Wildfire Smoke and Sustainable Product Choice
eligible_reason: Each wildfire is a separate 2x2-style DiD with a single common onset date (Camp Fire onset week of Nov 10 2018; the August 2020 fires use the same Treat x Post design in Table 5): Post_t is a common calendar dummy and Treat_s is a PM2.5 >= 55.5 threshold group indicator, so there are no unit-specific adoption dates. In addition the samples are propensity-score/covariate matched, the main specification includes time-varying marketing controls (relative price, feature share, assortment share), and several tables use triple interactions with Sustainable_p and product-store FE. The 2023 Canadian wildfire study is a survey.
design_notes: Table 2 (store-month, dish soap, 2018 Camp Fire, matched sample, 264 stores, N = 3,168): outcome = market share of Safer Choice sustainable dish soap; Treat_s x Post_t = .008 (.003), p = .008; store FE, month FE, time-varying controls X_st; SE clustered by store. Figure 5 event study (t = -5..6, ref t = 0 = month before exposure) shares the same single onset and includes controls. Tables 3-5 product-store level with Treat x Post x Sustainable triple interactions (ineligible). Robustness includes beta regression, generalized synthetic control, continuous PM2.5 intensity.
estimators_reported: TWFE DiD on matched sample with controls
screener_notes: Ineligible: common onset date per event, matching, time-varying controls, triple-diff. Data: NielsenIQ Kilts retail scanner (licensed) plus EPA PM2.5 (public) plus an online survey for the 2023 Canadian wildfires; no package in batch.
